facts.text: Sunset Heights earned its name because it sits on the high land west of Houston, where the trolley line ended.
In 1891, entrepreneur Richard Rodgers purchased 100 acres for $18,750—about $13 per 3,000‑square‑foot lot—to create the neighborhood.
The same year, Rodgers also founded the nearby Houston Heights, marking the start of a new residential district.
The Sunset Heights Neighborhood Association began offering guided tours of historic homes in 2003, inviting residents to explore the area’s past.
Because of its historic status, Sunset Heights residents must follow a strict building code that preserves the neighborhood’s architectural character.
The land that became Sunset Heights was first crossed by the Houston and Texas Central railroad in 1859, though the line faced bankruptcy by 1888.
